# ⬆️ dsh-codemod
> **Renamed:** previously `dsh-plugin-upgrade`; now **`dsh-codemod`**. Old repo stays as a pointer/b
ackup. New home: https://github.com/PerryLink/dsh-codemod
> **Non-official companion tool.** Part of the DSH standards family; not a certification, accreditat
ion, security audit, or official endorsement. Standard: https://github.com/PerryLink/dsh-standards.
The `dsh.standards` block is a `not-run` placeholder, not a pass.
> **Scope: three closed corridors, ending at `0.2.x`.** `legAB` = `0.1.3-alpha.1` → `0.1.5-rc.1`, `l
egC` = `0.1.5-rc.2` → `0.1.6-alpha.2`, `legD` = `0.1.6-alpha.2 / 0.1.7` → `0.2.x` (measured against
the `0.2.2-alpha.2` checkout and the guide's `0.2.1-alpha.2` baseline). The corridor cards stop at t
heir measured seams: `legD` scans five (`D1`–`D5`) and lists the rest of the 0.2 breakage as **advis
ory (not scanned)** — a clean scan is not a 0.2 compatibility certificate. For routine bundle update
s, use the host plugin manager's native `updateBundle()`.
- **1024 store channel**: `npm i -g dsh1024` once, then `dsh1024 plugin --profile web add dsh-codemo
d` (counts toward the deepseek1024.com install ranking).
**Plugin upgrade skill for DeepSeek Harness — one package, one corridor index, three closed corridor

## What is dsh-codemod?
Plugin upgrade skill for DeepSeek Harness — one package, one corridor index, three closed corridors:
The scanner routes itself: it reads the target repository's declared dsh band (or takes `--span`), t
hen applies that corridor's own evidence-bound catalog — `legAB`'s 20 seams (leg A `0.1.3-alpha.1` →
`D1`–`D5`). One entry point, so a client half that stopped mounting silently is never mistaken for "
typecheck is green".
*Workflow overview: call → plugin → result. The examples below use the real command surface.*
## Compatibility
| Surface | Status |
| Harness | DeepSeek Harness `dsh-v0.2.2-alpha.2` (measured checkout `ce7073d512`; guide baseline `d
sh-v0.2.1-alpha.2` = `d743267`). The corridor index is evidence-bound to the spans it measured: `leg
AB` = `0.1.3-alpha.1 → 0.1.5-rc.1` (tag `dsh-v0.1.7-alpha.2` = `183f08e9c6dd`; leg A→B handoff `dsh-
and `legD` = `0.1.6-alpha.2 / 0.1.7 → 0.2.x` (`0.2.2-alpha.2`). Peer band `@deepseek-ai/dsh-skill >

`@deepseek-ai/schemastery ^3.18.5-alpha.1`. |
| Node | `^22.19.0 \|\| >=24.0.0` |
| Platforms | Anyw

here Node runs; the scanner is filesystem-only and platform-neutral |
| Model | Text-only models ful

ly supported; the skill is a Markdown body, no tool or vision requirement |
| Corridor index | One p
ackage, one entry point. `lib/route.mjs` holds the closed corridors and the CLI routes to the matchi
ng one from the target repo's declared band (`engines.dsh`, the `@deepseek-ai/dsh*` ranges); `--span
legAB\|legC\|legD` overrides the guess and an undeclared band falls back to the oldest corridor. Th
e three catalogs are never merged: each corridor keeps its own seam array, card, evidence, fixtures

and parity gate. |
| Scope | **Three closed corridors**: `legAB` = `0.1.3-alpha.1` → `0.1.5-rc.1` (l
5 scanned seams + an explicit advisory section). A corridor never widens: a hop that adds a seam is

a new corridor — a new card and a new index row, not a new package. |
| Legs | Every leg lives in th
is package: leg A keeps the `S1`–`S10` + `M1` seams, leg B keeps `C1`, `C2`, `C4`, `C5`, `H1`–`H4`,
`P1`, leg C keeps `E1`–`E5`, and leg D keeps `D1`–`D5` — each with its own evidence, card section, f

ixtures and rollback path. There is no sibling package to install. |
[该节后续省略]
## What you get
Two halves, one seam catalog per corridor:
- **A bundled agent skill (`plugin-upgrade`)** — the corridor cards and a fix-and-verify loop. The b
ody first routes the caller to the corridor that matches its peer band; the model loads it only when

a task actually needs it, and the package contributes no system-prompt paragraph and no tool.
- **A
zero-dependency CLI (`dsh-codemod`; legacy alias `dsh-plugin-upgrade-scan`)** — resolves the corrid
or and reports `file:line` facts for that corridor's seams: `legAB`'s twenty (`S3`, `S8`, `S9`, `M1`
e-read from the harness tag ranges on 2026-09-09 (leg A) and 2026-09-10 (leg B), `legC`'s five (`E1`
–`E5`) measured on `dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.2` (2026-09-19), or `legD`'s five (`D1`–`D5`) re-read on 2026-1
1-01 against the `0.2.2-alpha.2` checkout (`ce7073d512`) and the guide's `0.2.1-alpha.2` baseline. E
xit `1` on any error-severity hit, so it drops straight into CI.
The point is the failure mode this corridor exists to kill: **this span's breakage is mostly silent,
from both ends.** The type line can be stale, so the repo compiles against the **old** catalog (sea
m `M1`), and the bare `conversation` client slot was deleted with no alias while `ctx.slots.inject()
` only runs its callback when the declaration exists — so a client half that still targets it stops
mounting with no error, no log line and no failed build (seam `C1`). Three classes of breakage survi
ve `typecheck` + `test`:
1. the local gate compiles a stale type line — old `paths` alias, or dev/test types pinned at `0.1.5

-alpha.*` (seam `M1`);
[该节后续省略]
## Security boundaries
- **Read-only scan.** The CLI never writes inside the scanned repository; `--json` writes only to th

e path you pass.
- **No network, no shell.** The scanner imports nothing beyond Node's standard libr

ary and never spawns a process.
- **No secrets.** Nothing in the package reads credentials, environm

ent tokens, or session data.
- **Sandboxed smoke recipe.** The card's real-host check uses a `mkdtem
p` `DSH_HOME`; it never touches your real `~/.dsh`.
